resources.readme_excerpt:
MailCheap

Newsletters where you pay for the emails you send, not for dormant subscribers.
A fraction of the price of beehiiv and the like.

Website · API docs · Sign up for MailCheap Cloud

![MailCheap's overview: emails sent, delivery, open, click, bounce and complaint rates, and subscribers over the last 30 days](docs/screenshots/overview.webp) MailCheap is a newsletter app: write an issue, send it to your list, publish it on the web, from the dashboard or from your AI agent. This repository is the whole app. Self-host it with your own Amazon SES or PostShiba account, or use [MailCheap Cloud](https://mailcheap.ai), which runs this same code. ## Features - **AI agents and the dashboard.** Everything the dashboard does also works from an AI agent through the MCP server, and from code through the REST API, with the same checks and limits. ChatGPT, Claude and Grok Bot connect with OAuth; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with an API key. MCP marks sending as an action that can't be undone, so agents ask you first. - **Write, review, send.** Write in an editor with slash commands, images and boxes, or send Markdown or a complete HTML email through the API and MCP. Review shows what to fix before sending: subject, preview text, unsubscribe link, Gmail's 100 KB clip, postal address, sender. Then send it, schedule it, or start with your most engaged readers and send to more later. - **Imports from beehiiv, Substack and Mailchimp.** Their CSV exports import as they are, with each reader's status and signup date, and so do Kit's, MailerLite's, Buttondown's, Ghost's and EmailOctopus's. - **A website for each newsletter**, on a free subdomain on MailCheap Cloud (`.mailcheap.ai`), or on your server: every issue gets a page search engines can find, with a signup form, an author page, share images and a sitemap. - **Sending from your own domain**, with the DKIM, return path and DMARC records to add and a check for each. On MailCheap Cloud, a newsletter without a domain sends from its own shared address, `hello@.mailcheap.ai`. - **Deliverability protections**, built in: - sending pace: contacts the account never emailed go out in steps, a random 2% first, then 5% more, then the rest, 30 minutes apart while their bounces and complaints stay low. On MailCheap Cloud, a domain new to Gmail also sends to its first 2,000 Gmail readers on its first day and to the others the next day; - list cleanup, on by default: readers who ignored several issues get one "do you still want this?" email, then stop getting issues; - contact cleaning: imports leave out invalid, misspelled (gmial.com), spam trap, role, throwaway and duplicate addresses, domains that can't receive email, and anyone who unsubscribed, bounced or complained before; - one never-email list for the whole server: an address the email provider says doesn't exist (for 180 days) or that turned out to be a spam trap (for good) is left out of every account's imports, signups and sends, and only a keyed hash of it is kept; - spam and bounce limits: a send pauses past 2.5% hard bounces or 0.08% complaints, and the account is blocked past 5% or 0.3%, or on a spam trap hit; - Gmail's spam rates, which Gmail never reports one complaint at a time: every email carries a `Feedback-ID` for Gmail's feedback loop (its campaign or newsletter, its account, its kind), and once an admin connects [Google Postmaster Tools](https://postmaster.google.com), MailCheap reads it every day. An account Gmail flags at 0.08% has its sends paused, at 0.3% it's blocked, and the admins hear when the whole domain reaches 0.1%; - one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) and a signed unsubscribe link in every email, and confirmed opt-in, on by default. - **Several newsletters**: up to 3 per account, each with its own contacts, campaigns and website. - **Signups and stats**: signup forms and a signup API, welcome emails, open and click tracking that leaves link scanners out, subscribers over time, and reports by inbox provider (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud...). | Write, review, send | The newsletter's website | | --- | --- | | ![The campaign editor's Write step: the subject, preview text and body of a draft, with the Write, Review and Send steps at the top](docs/screenshots/editor.webp) | ![A newsletter's website: its signup form, a featured issue and the latest issues](docs/screenshots/website.webp) | All names and addresses in the screenshots are made up. ## MailCheap Cloud or self-hosted | | [MailCheap Cloud](https://mailcheap.ai) | Self-hosted | | --- | --- | --- | | Price | From $19 a month for 20,000 emails | Free, plus what your provider charges per email: $0.10 to $0.16 per 1,000 on Amazon SES | | Sending | Set up for you, from `hello@.mailcheap.ai` or your domain | Your Amazon SES or PostShiba account, from your domain | | Website | `.mailcheap.ai` | `/archive/` on your server's domain | | Who signs in | Anyone who signs up | The emails you allow | | Limits | Emails a month and active subscribers, by plan | None | | Setup | A few minutes | About an hour, most of it waiting for DNS and production access | | Support | A chat in the dashboard | None: issues are off | MailCheap Cloud is this repository with `MAILCHEAP_CLOUD=true`, which adds open sign-up, plans and Stripe billing. Only active subscribers count toward a plan, not the ones list cleanup marked dormant. Its marketing site (the landing, pricing and legal pages) isn't part of the open source. Every change to the app ships to both. With your own sending account, you pay your provider for the emails you send: 10,000 readers and 4 issues a month is 40,000 emails, about $4 to $6 on Amazon SES. ## Self-hosting [![Deploy with Vercel](https://vercel.com/button)](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmarclou%2Fmailcheap&project-name=mailcheap&repository-name=mailcheap&env=MONGODB_URI,BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,SUPPRESSION_HASH_KEY,ADMIN_EMAILS,EMAIL_FROM&envDescription=Database%2C%20a%20signing%20secret%20and%20a%20hash%20key%20%2832%2B%20characters%20each%3A%20openssl%20rand%20-base64%2048%29%2C%20your%20email%20to%20sign%20in%20with%2C%20and%20the%20from%20address%20of%20sign-in%20codes.%20Add%20RESEND_API_KEY%2C%20or%20set%20up%20SES%20or%20PostShiba%2C%20so%20the%20codes%20can%20reach%20you.&envLink=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmarclou%2Fmailcheap%23environment-variables) Plan for about an hour, most of it waiting for DNS and for your provider to approve production sending. Self-hosting comes without support: issues are off and setup questions go unanswered. ### What you need | Service | For | Cost | | --- | --- | --- | | [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas) | Contacts, campaigns, stats | Free tier works | | [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/) or [PostShiba](https://postshiba.com) | Sending | SES: $0.10 to $0.16 per 1,000 emails, depending on its pricing plan. PostShiba: a fixed price per cluster, invite only for now | | [Upstash QStash](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash) | Background sending and scheduling | Free tier to start, then pay per message. One message sends 50 emails | | [Vercel](https://vercel.com) or any Node.js 22+ host | Hosting | Free tier works | | [Resend](https://resend.com) (optional) | Sign-in codes and alerts. Without it, they go through SES or PostShiba | Free plan works | | [Upstash Redis](https://upstash.com/docs/redis) (optional) | Rate limits shared by every server instance | Free tier | | [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/) with [CloudFront](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/), or [Vercel Blob](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob) (optional) | Image uploads in the editor, the newsletter settings and the API | S3 and CloudFront: pay per use. Blob: free tier | Without Redis, MailCheap counts the same rate limits in each server instance's memory. That still stops a script hammering a form, but on serverless hosts the limits aren't shared between instances and reset on each deploy. Add Redis before you put a signup form on a busy site. Without S3 or Blob, image uploads are off; HTML and Markdown campaigns can still use images hosted anywhere. ### Environment variables | Variable | What it does | | --- | --- | | `MONGODB_URI` | MongoDB connection string with a database name | | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Signs sessions and every link in sent emails. 32+ random characters (`openssl rand -base64 48`), or the server refuses to start. Rotating it signs everyone out and breaks links in emails already sent | | `SUPPRESSION_HASH_KEY` | Keys the hashes of the never-email list every account shares. 32+ random characters of its own, never `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, or the server refuses to start, after an upgrade too. Changing it empties the list | | `ADMIN_EMAILS` | Comma-separated emails that can sign in and open `/admin` | | `ALLOWED_EMAILS` | Who else can sign in: addresses and `@domain` entries, comma-separated | | `EMAIL_FROM` | From address of sign-in codes and alerts, on a domain your Resend account or email provider verified | | `APP_URL` | Public URL of the app, for email links and sign-in. On Vercel it defaults to the production domain | | `RESEND_API_KEY` | Optional: sign-in codes and alerts through Resend. Without it, they go through the email provider | | `SENDING_ENABLED` | Nothing goes to readers unless it's `true`. Sign-in codes and alerts don't wait for it | | `SES_*` or `POSTSHIBA_*` | The email provider, in step 4 | | `QSTASH_*` | Background sending and scheduling, in step 5 | [`.env.example`](.env.example) lists every variable with what it does, the optional ones included: Google sign-in and Postmaster Tools, image uploads, Redis, Telegram alerts, the shared domain, and MailCheap Cloud's own. ### 1. Database 1. Create a free cluster on [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas). 2. **Database Access**: add a user with a password and the "Read and write to any database" role. 3. **Network Access**: allow `0.0.0.0/0`. Vercel doesn't have fixed IP addresses. 4. **Connect > Drivers**: copy the connection string and add a database name before the `?`, like `...mongodb.net/mailcheap?retryWrites=true`. That's your `MONGODB_URI`. ### 2. Deploy 1. Click **Deploy** above. 2. Fill in `MONGODB_URI`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (at least 32 characters; generate it with `openssl rand -base64 48`), `SUPPRESSION_HASH_KEY` (generated the same way, another value), `ADMIN_EMAILS` (your email) and `EMAIL_FROM` (like `MailCheap `, on a domain your Resend account or email provider verified). With a short secret, MailCheap refuses to start and the logs say why. 3. Sign-in codes need a way to reach you. The quickest is [Resend](https://resend.com): verify `EMAIL_FROM`'s domain there and add `RESEND_API_KEY`. Without it, codes go through SES or PostShiba once step 4 is done. 4. Open `https://.vercel.app/signin` and sign in with your email. Sending stays off until you finish the next steps, so nothing goes out to readers by mistake. On any other Node.js host: `npm ci && npm run build && npm start`, with the same variables, behind HTTPS. `/api/health` answers 200, or 503 with what to fix. If you plan to use your own domain for the dashboard (like `mailcheap.example.com`), add it in Vercel now and set `APP_URL` to it. Links in your emails use `APP_URL`, so it should be final before your first send. ### 3. Who can sign in Only the emails you list: `ADMIN_EMAILS` (who can also open `/admin`) and `ALLOWED_EMAILS`, a comma-separated list of addresses and whole domains, like `jane@example.com, @example.org`. It's checked at every sign-in, with a code or with Google, and anyone you take off the list is signed out and loses their API keys at their next request. With both lists empty, nobody can sign in. Everyone gets an account of their own, with up to 3 newsletters and their contacts and campaigns, and the account's domains and API keys. There's no billing on a self-hosted server: no plans, no limits. ### 4. Email provider Pick Amazon SES or PostShiba (invite only for now). `EMAIL_PROVIDER` picks one; without it, MailCheap uses PostShiba when `POSTSHIBA_API_KEY` is set and SES otherwise. Every account gets its own tenant there, with its own domains, suppression list and pause switch. MailCheap creates them; you set up the provider account and its events once. #### Amazon SES Use one AWS region for everything below (the examples use `us-east-1`). An AWS account just for MailCheap is best: SES reputation and limits are per AWS account. 1. **Request production access.** New accounts are in the sandbox (200 emails a day, verified recipients only). In **Account dashboard > Request production access**, pick Marketing, and explain that readers opt in, that bounces and complaints are suppressed automatically, and that every email has one-click unsubscribe. AWS usually answers within a day. 2. **Create an SNS topic** for events, like `mailcheap-ses-events`, and switch it to signature version 2, which signs messages with SHA256 instead of SHA1: `aws sns set-topic-attributes --topic-arn --attribute-name SignatureVersion --attribute-value 2`. Then **Create subscription** with protocol HTTPS and endpoint `https:///api/webhooks/ses`, raw message delivery off. MailCheap confirms the subscription by itself once it's deployed with the variables of step 4. 3. **Create an IAM user for MailCheap** with this policy, then create an access key for it: ```json { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "ses:SendEmail", "ses:GetAccount", "ses:CreateTenant", "ses:GetTenant", "ses:DeleteTenant", "ses:TagResource", "ses:CreateTenantResourceAssociation", "ses:DeleteTenantResourceAssociation", "ses:UpdateReputationEntityPolicy", "ses:UpdateReputationEntityCustomerManagedStatus", "ses:CreateConfigurationSet", "ses:CreateConfigurationSetEventDestination", "ses:DeleteConfigurationSet", "ses:CreateEmailIdentity", "ses:GetEmailIdentity", "ses:PutEmailIdentityMailFromAttributes", "ses:DeleteEmailIdentity" ], "Resource": "*" } ] } ``` 4. **Add the variables** and redeploy: `SES_REGION`, `SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `SES_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` (the 12-digit account ID) and `SES_SNS_TOPIC_ARN`. Each account's configuration set publishes its events to that topic. 5. **Optional: tenant pauses.** SES pauses tenants that send badly. To block the account in MailCheap too, send SES's tenant status and reputation finding events from EventBridge to a second SNS topic, subscribe `https:///api/webhooks/ses-tenants` to it, and set `SES_TENANT_SNS_TOPIC_ARN`. Without Resend, sign-in codes and alerts go out through SES from `EMAIL_FROM`, outside every tenant, so its domain has to be verified in the AWS account before your first sign-in: **Identities > Create identity > Domain**, with Easy DKIM. In the sandbox, the addresses you sign in with have to be verified too. #### PostShiba PostShiba approves production sending by hand: until then, sends to anyone outside your team answer `kyc_required` (campaigns pause with that reason) and a team can have one cluster. 1. **Team and key.** In API keys, create a full access key: `POSTSHIBA_API_KEY`, with the team id as `POSTSHIBA_TEAM_ID`. Add a payment method (clusters need one). 2. **Clusters.** One `bulk` cluster sends every email: its id goes in `POSTSHIBA_BULK_CLUSTER_ID`. Later, a `transactional` cluster in `POSTSHIBA_TRANSACTIONAL_CLUSTER_ID` takes welcome, confirmation and test emails, so they never wait behind a campaign. Set `SEND_RATE_PER_SECOND` to the bulk cluster's hourly cap divided by 3,600, less what welcome and test emails need when they share it. At a cap, PostShiba answers `throttled`: the batch goes back to the queue and QStash brings it after the hour. 3. **Webhook.** One endpoint for the whole team (no cluster or tenant) at `https:///api/webhooks/postshiba` with the events `processed`, `delivered`, `deferred`, `bounce`, `dropped`, `spamreport` and `unsubscribe`. Its secret goes in `POSTSHIBA_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. 4. **Encryption key.** `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, generated once with `openssl rand -base64 32`. It encrypts each tenant's SMTP password, and Postmaster Tools' refresh token. MailCheap creates the rest: a tenant per account (slug `mc-`), an SMTP credential for it on each cluster (one in all on a single cluster), and its domains. Creating credentials and domains and running domain checks share PostShiba's budget of 60 an hour per key; a failed setup is retried at the account's next send. Without Resend, sign-in codes and alerts go through a tenant of their own, `mc-platform`, on the transactional cluster. The first one adds `EMAIL_FROM`'s domain there, and the server log lists the two CNAME records it needs; once PostShiba finds them, codes go out. A domain belongs to one tenant at PostShiba, so `EMAIL_FROM` needs a domain or subdomain that no newsletter sends from. ### 5. QStash 1. In the [Upstash console](https://console.upstash.com/qstash), open QStash and copy `QSTASH_TOKEN`, `QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY` and `QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY` (and `QSTASH_URL` if you picked a region other than the default). 2. Add them and redeploy. QStash calls `APP_URL/api/jobs/...` to send each batch, so the app has to be reachable on the internet. MailCheap checks QStash's signature on every job. ### 6. Turn sending on 1. In MailCheap, open **Domains** and add the domain your newsletter sends from. Use a subdomain like `mail.example.com`, so your main domain's email is unaffected. Add the DNS records it lists (DKIM, return path, and DMARC if your root domain has none), set to DNS only if your DNS is on Cloudflare, then click **Check now**. 2. Create your newsletter. The from address must be on that domain, and the postal address shows in every email's footer (anti-spam laws require one). 3. Set `SENDING_ENABLED=true` and redeploy. 4. Write a campaign, send yourself a test, then send. A first send to new contacts goes out in steps by itself; for a new domain, also set a limit to reach your most engaged readers first, and use **Send to more** on the report once the first step looks healthy. ### Optional - **Google sign-in.** Create an OAuth client (web application) with the redirect URI `/api/auth/callback/google`, then set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`. The allowlist applies, and a Google sign-in joins an existing user only when Google verified that email. - **Gmail's spam rates (Google Postmaster Tools).** It needs the Google sign-in client above, `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `CRON_SECRET`; without them, or until someone connects, nothing runs. 1. In the client's Google Cloud project, enable the **Gmail Postmaster Tools API**, and add `/api/admin/postmaster/callback` to the client's authorized redirect URIs. Its consent screen has to be published (In production): in Testing, Google expires the connection after 7 days. 2. At [postmaster.google.com](https://postmaster.google.com), add the domain every email is DKIM-signed with: `SHARED_DOMAIN`, which PostShiba's primary domain signing adds to every email, or `POSTMASTER_DOMAIN`. A domain the same Google account verified in Search Console is verified already. 3. On `/admin`, under **Gmail spam rates**, click **Connect** and allow access with that Google account. Google warns that it hasn't verified the app: it's your own, continue. MailCheap asks for read access to traffic statistics only, and stores the refresh token encrypted with `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Vercel Cron then runs `/api/cron/postmaster` every day (`vercel.json`); elsewhere, have a scheduler call it with `Authorization: Bearer `. It acts on the newest day of Gmail's data once, with the thresholds in `POSTMASTER` (`lib/config.js`). Gmail only reports domains that send to at least 50 Gmail users a day, and a feedback ID once it has enough emails and spam reports, so until then it finds nothing and says nothing. If Google refuses the connection, one alert says so. Every email's `Feedback-ID` is `:mc-::mailcheap` (`lib/sending-rules.js`): SES sends it as it is, and PostShiba writes its own in its place, also led by `mc-`, so each ID maps back to its account (`lib/postmaster-rules.js`). - **Image uploads.** The quickest is Vercel Blob: in Vercel, **Storage > Create > Blob**, connect it to the project, and redeploy. To serve images from a subdomain of your own (like `cdn.example.com`), put an S3 bucket behind CloudFront. It takes over new uploads, and images already on Blob keep their URLs: 1. Create a private S3 bucket with Block Public Access on. 2. In ACM, request a certificate for the subdomain in `us-east-1`, validated by DNS. If your domain has CAA records, add `0 issue "amazon.com"`. 3. Create a CloudFront distribution: the bucket as origin through Origin Access Control (add the bucket policy CloudFront gives you), viewer protocol HTTPS only, the CachingOptimized cache policy, and the subdomain as alternate domain name with that certificate. Point the subdomain at the distribution with a CNAME. 4. Create an IAM user for MailCheap with this policy, then an access key for it. Deleting an account deletes its images and clears them from CloudFront's cache, hence `s3:DeleteObject` and `cloudfront:CreateInvalidation`: ```json { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:GetObject", "s3:DeleteObject"], "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::/accounts/*" }, { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["cloudfront:CreateInvalidation"], "Resource": "arn:aws:cloudfront:::distribution/" } ] } ``` 5. Set `IMAGES_S3_BUCKET`, `IMAGES_S3_REGION`, `IMAGES_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `IMAGES_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `IMAGES_CDN_URL` (like `https://cdn.example.com`) and `IMAGES_CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID` (the distribution's ID), and redeploy. Builds read `IMAGES_CDN_URL` too. Each image gets a name that never changes and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so CloudFront and browsers keep it for a year. An account's purge invalidates its folder, `/accounts//*`, on the distribution, so CloudFront stops serving its deleted images. - **Shared rate limits.** Create a Redis database in the [Upstash console](https://console.upstash.com/redis) and add `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`. - **Alerts on Telegram.** Every admin alert shows on `/admin`, and the ones an admin can act on are an email to `ADMIN_EMAILS` too. The others only show on `/admin`: an admin's own block, shared addresses waiting for the DNS helper, whose own alert covers them, and the email provider refusing one account's login, unless a second account's is refused within the hour. The ones that need someone (an automatic account block, the email provider refusing MailCheap's sends, holding a tenant or refusing a customer's own domain, Gmail's spam rate for the domain reaching 0.1% or Postmaster Tools refusing the connection, sign-in codes, Stripe events, webhooks or background jobs failing, QStash refusing jobs, shared addresses and the DNS helper) can reach Telegram too: create a bot with [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather), send it a message, and set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and the chat's id as `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`. Each alert goes there at most once every 6 hours. A customer with a plan whose emails the provider refuses (a domain it suspended or holds, or their sending space) can't fix it from their dashboard: each campaign it pauses, and each newsletter whose signup or test emails it refuses, alerts, and `/admin` lists them first in Needs a look, in red, with blocked accounts that have a plan. Replies to the owner's own email about such a refusal, or about their account's block, go to `URGENT_REPLY_TO` when it's set, an admin's own inbox. On PostShiba, have a scheduler call `/api/cron/hourly` every hour with `Authorization: Bearer ` (Vercel Cron sends it once `CRON_SECRET` is set): it checks the team's status (a suspension, the approval, clusters at their cap, held tenants) and the sending domains it suspended or holds that a customer with a plan sends from, and alerts on what stops sending, and looks at each verified sending domain's DNS records once a day, so a record that's gone or behind a proxy stops that domain and emails its owner. It also ends the imports whose upload stopped, a browser closed halfway, and their owners see it in the dashboard's notifications. Its first run with Telegram set up posts "Telegram alerts are on". - **Shared domain.** `SHARED_DOMAIN` is how MailCheap Cloud gives every newsletter without a domain of its own

resources.readme_excerpt:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 7 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 7 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 7. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/claude-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? Browse the [Showcase](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/showcase) for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix. - Product launch videos and feature announcements - PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions - Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations - Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music - Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers - Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines ## Frame.md **frame.md — your design system, ready for video.** Every brand has a `design.md`. None of them were written for a camera. `frame.md` is the missing translation layer: it takes your web-context design spec and inverts it for the frame — the same tokens, the same rules, but rewritten so an AI agent can compose a promo video without guessing at scale or reaching for web chrome. The output is a `DESIGN.md` superset your whole toolchain can read. Atoms stay sacred. Composition stays free. Numbers come from the script.

Biennale Yellow
BlockFrame

Blue Professional
Bold Poster

Broadside
Capsule

Cartesian
Cobalt Grid

Coral
Creative Mode
Browse and remix them all at [hyperframes.studio/design](https://hyperframes.studio/design). ## How It Works Define a video as HTML. Add data attributes for timing and tracks. Use GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or your own frame adapter for seekable animation. ```html

Launch day

``` Preview instantly in the browser. Render locally or in Docker. The renderer seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes the result with FFmpeg, so the same input produces the same video. ## HyperFrames Stack HyperFrames is the open-source rendering engine, plus a growing set of tools around HTML-native video creation. | Piece | Status | What it does | | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | CLI | Available | Scaffold, preview, lint, inspect, and render local video projects | | Core / Engine / Producer | Available | Parse compositions, drive headless Chrome, encode video, and mix audio | | Catalog | Available | Reusable blocks and components for transitions, overlays, captions, charts, maps, and effects | | Agent skills | Available | Teach coding agents the video-production patterns that generic web docs miss | | Studio | Available, evolving | Browser surface for previewing and editing compositions | | AWS Lambda rendering | Available | Deploy a distributed render stack and drive renders from your laptop or CI | | [hyperframes.studio](https://hyperframes.studio/) | Available | Community playground for previewing, iterating, sharing, and rendering HTML-native video projects | | [frame.md](https://hyperframes.studio/design) | Available | Invert your design system for the camera — a DESIGN.md superset an agent can compose video from | ## Catalog Install ready-to-use blocks and components: ```bash npx hyperframes add flash-through-white # shader transition npx hyperframes add instagram-follow # social overlay npx hyperframes add data-chart # animated chart ``` Browse the catalog at [hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/blocks/data-chart). ## Why HyperFrames? - **HTML-native:** compositions are HTML files with data attributes. No React requirement, no proprietary timeline format. - **Agent-friendly:** agents already write HTML, and the CLI is non-interactive by default. - **Deterministic:** same input, same frames, same output. Built for CI, regression tests, and automated rendering. - **No build step:** an `index.html` composition plays as-is and can be previewed directly in the browser. - **Adapter-based animation:** bring GSAP, CSS animations, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or a custom runtime. - **Open source:** Apache 2.0 license, with no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds. ## HyperFrames vs Remotion HyperFrames is inspired by [Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev). Both tools render video with headless Chrome and FFmpeg. The main difference is the authoring model: Remotion's bet is React components; HyperFrames' bet is plain HTML that humans and agents can both write easily. | | **HyperFrames** | **Remotion** | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | | Authoring | HTML + CSS + seekable animation | React components | | Build step | None; `index.html` plays as-is | Bundler required | | Agent handoff | Plain HTML files | JSX / React project | | Library-clock animations | Seekable, frame-accurate via adapters | Wall-clock animation patterns need care | | Distributed rendering | Local and AWS Lambda render paths | Remotion Lambda, mature cloud renderer | | License | Apache 2.0 | Source-available Remotion License | Read the full comparison in the [HyperFrames vs Remotion guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/hyperframes-vs-remotion). ## Documentation Full documentation: [hyperframes.heygen.com/introduction](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/introduction) - [Quickstart](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/quickstart) - [Showcase](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/showcase) - [Guides](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/gsap-animation) - [API Reference](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/packages/core) - [Catalog](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/blocks/data-chart) - [Examples](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/examples) - [AWS Lambda rendering](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/deploy/aws-lambda) ## Packages | Package | Description | | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | [`hyperframes`](packages/cli) | CLI for creating, previewing, linting, and rendering compositions | | [`@hyperframes/core`](packages/core) | Types, parsers, generators, linter, runtime, and frame adapters | | [`@hyperframes/engine`](packages/engine) | Seekable page-to-video capture engine using Puppeteer and FFmpeg | | [`@hyperframes/producer`](packages/producer) | Full rendering pipeline for capture, encode, and audio mix | | [`@hyperframes/studio`](packages/studio) | Browser-based composition editor UI | | [`@hyperframes/player`](packages/player) | Embeddable `` web component | | [`@hyperframes/shader-transitions`](packages/shader-transitions) | WebGL shader transitions for compositions | | [`@hyperframes/aws-lambda`](packages/aws-lambda) | AWS Lambda SDK and deployment surface for distributed renders | ## Community HyperFrames is used in production at [HeyGen](https://www.heygen.com), with community examples from teams like [tldraw](https://tldraw.com), [TanStack](https://tanstack.com), and others in [ADOPTERS.md](ADOPTERS.md). Open a PR if your team is using HyperFrames. - Questions and ideas: [Discord](https://discord.gg/EbK98HBPdk) - Bugs and feature requests: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/issues) - User research: [Book a casual 30-minute conversation with the HyperFrames team](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/appointments/schedules/AcZssZ2cSpKoDgmcmRrgekrnrgqmvPT8W6F2Zg6e7MY7IJqaZKwpn_I0NdTHkN390iguMepE_NVg8ezb?gv=true) — no preparation or sales pitch - Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) - Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Development Note The repo uses [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com) for golden regression-test baselines under `packages/producer/tests/**/output.mp4` (about 240 MB of `.mp4` files). If you're cloning the full repo for development, install Git LFS first: ```bash # macOS brew install git-lfs # Ubuntu / Debian sudo apt install git-lfs # Windows winget install GitHub.GitLFS # Then, once per machine git lfs install ``` If you only need source files, you can skip LFS content: ```bash GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes.git ``` ## License [Apache 2.0](LICENSE)

---
name: figma
description: Bring Figma into a HyperFrames video - rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion (frames read as states, not slides), shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when the person pastes a figma.com link or asks to use a Figma design, frame, logo or brand.
---

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin.

# Figma → HyperFrames

Every import happens at build time and freezes a local file with its source recorded under `.media/`, so renders never call Figma and re-running a command re-imports only what changed. Assets, tokens and components go over REST with a token; motion and shader data need a Figma connector, or a native export from the person.

## Access

`FIGMA_TOKEN` in the shell or the project `.env`. Check it exists before the first command; if not, tell the person how to make one and stop: figma.com → Settings → Security → Personal access tokens, read-only **File content** and **File metadata**, plus **Library content** for `tokens` on non-Enterprise plans. They set it themselves; never ask them to paste it into the chat.

| Error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `BAD_TOKEN` (401) | Expired or revoked: make a new one |
| `FORBIDDEN` (403) | The message names the missing scope, or the file isn't visible to the account |
| `REQUIRES_ENTERPRISE` (403, variables) | Not a failure: the published-styles fallback already ran |
| `RATE_LIMITED` (429) | Already retried with backoff; wait a minute or import fewer nodes per call |

## Commands

- A layer, logo or image: `npx hyperframes figma asset '<url or fileKey:nodeId>' [more refs] --format svg|png --scale 2 --description "<what it is>" [--entity "<brand mark>"]`. SVG for vectors and logos, PNG at 2x for raster. Several nodes of one file in one call render in a single request; `--entity` lets `/media-use` find a brand mark later.
- Brand colours and type: `npx hyperframes figma tokens <fileKey>`. Run it before `component` and paste the printed entries into `data-composition-variables`. Without Enterprise it falls back to published styles. A connector can supply variables there instead: cache its raw response in `.media/figma-cache/` and write the bindings to `.media/figma-bindings.jsonl` (`{kind:"binding", figmaId, sourceFileKey, compositionVariableId:"figma:<name>", version}`).
- A frame as editable HTML at exact geometry: `npx hyperframes figma component '<url or fileKey:nodeId>'`, packaged under `compositions/components/<name>/`. A fill bound to an imported token comes out as `var(--slug, #literal)`, so one variable re-brands every import; an unknown token stays a literal marked `data-figma-unresolved`: import that library's tokens and re-import. Ask once which file a library is; never match by hex.
- Check hero components against Figma's pixels (`figma asset <same node> --format png`). Text drift is the usual cause; report drift you can't fix instead of hand-tweaking the import.

## Motion (connector)

Usage beacon: these phases have no CLI touchpoint, so run `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion` when you begin and `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion --event=skill_completed --outcome=success|error` when done. Same for shaders (`figma-shaders`) and storyboards (`figma-storyboard`).

1. Fetch motion context for the parent frame in one recursive request; cache the raw JSON in `.media/figma-cache/`.
2. Normalise with `motionContextToDocs(raw, { selectorFor, repeat })` from `@hyperframes/core/figma`, never by transcribing keyframes. It reads the motion.dev snippets (the CSS snippets stretch durations), drops loop-wrap tail keyframes and keeps bezier eases. `selectorFor` returns the ids from the component import.
3. `motionToGsap(doc)` → `emitTimelineScript(spec)`, injected after the GSAP and CustomEase tags: paused, finite, a literal `window.__timelines` key. Named eases outside the mapped set fall back to linear; say so.
4. Verify against Figma's own export: `node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/verify-motion.mjs --reference <export.mp4> --render <render.mp4> --crop WxH+X+Y`. It compares motion between samples, so static drift cancels out, and fails under 15 dB (faithful ≈ 20+, diverging ≈ 5). Measure `--crop` from the render's card edges. A fail means fix the translation, not the threshold.
5. A track that won't translate: export it, freeze the MP4 and place it as `<video class="clip">`.

## Shaders

Figma's export path flattens shaders to their base colour, and shader source is only reachable for library-published styles. Ask the person for a native export of that frame (PNG or MP4) and place it as an asset or clip.

## Storyboards: frames are KEYFRAMES, not slides

Two frames holding the same element describe that element's state through time: animate the element between the states. Playing the frames back to back as stills is the failure mode.

1. Scenes are every frame-sized node in the section, named frames and loose full-frame rectangles alike: filter by size, not type or name. Order by `absoluteBoundingBox.x`.
2. Match children across neighbouring frames by name first, then by similar size and position. Tween geometry between states; crossfade two exports in place when the pixels changed. Export one asset per element, not one still per frame. Unmatched children enter or exit at their scene's beat.
3. Text nodes below the strip are motion notes for the scene above them, not on-screen copy. A note about motion inside a scene ("lines reveal one after another") means import that frame as a component and animate it.
4. Export in batches of about 4 scene frames per call: past about 12 ids `/v1/images` times out.
5. Frames that are one product UI in successive states: rebuild the UI as live DOM: code what changes state, freeze what doesn't, and treat each frame change as an interaction to perform (the cursor moves, clicks, the screen responds), not a tween to apply.
6. Stills are the fallback, only for frames with no shared elements.

Never leave a Figma URL in the composition.

metadata.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, Qoder, and Pi. 45 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.

resources.readme_excerpt:
**An agent skill that draws diagrams as one self-contained HTML + SVG file, in your brand.
45 diagram types. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.** [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/cathrynlavery/diagram-design?style=flat-square&color=bf4520)](https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design/stargazers) [![skills.sh installs](https://skills.sh/b/cathrynlavery/diagram-design?style=flat-square)](https://skills.sh/cathrynlavery/diagram-design/diagram-design) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/cathrynlavery/diagram-design/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Plugin version](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fcathrynlavery%2Fdiagram-design%2Fmain%2F.claude-plugin%2Fplugin.json&query=%24.version&label=version&style=flat-square&color=555555)](CHANGELOG.md) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-555555?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **[Website](https://diagramdesign.dev) · [Gallery](https://cathrynlavery.github.io/diagram-design/) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)** [Install](#install) · [What it makes](#what-it-makes) · [Quickstart](#quickstart) · [Match your brand](#onboarding-make-it-look-like-your-brand) · [Import](#import-from-drawio-mermaid-or-excalidraw) · [Export](#export-to-png--svg) · [Contributing](#contributing) npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design


Ask your agent in plain words: - *"Make me an architecture diagram of my app: frontend, backend, database, Redis cache."* - *"I need a quadrant showing Q2 projects by impact vs effort."* - *"Give me a sequence of a bearer call with token refresh on 401."* - *"Onboard diagram-design to https://yoursite.com"* (pulls your palette and fonts so every diagram after this one matches your site) The agent picks the type, states its plan, and writes one `.html` file you can open by double-clicking. --- ## Install Works with any host that reads Agent Skills, including Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Qoder, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Cline, Windsurf and Amp: ```bash npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design ``` In Claude Code, the plugin marketplace gets you updates and the slash commands: ```text /plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design /plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design ``` Official builds come only from this repository. LittleMight, Cathryn Lavery's company, publishes the plugin directory listings; a listing under any other name is an unofficial copy. [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) lists what the skill sends over the network.
Claude Code: turn on auto-update After installing, run `/plugin`, open **Marketplaces**, select **diagram-design**, and choose **Enable auto-update**. Claude Code disables auto-update by default for third-party marketplaces; after this toggle, it refreshes the marketplace and installed plugin in the background after startup. Run `/reload-plugins` when prompted, or let the next session load the update.
Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Amp, Zed, Warp, Roo, Kilo and other Agent Skills hosts The cross-agent [`skills` CLI](https://skills.sh) resolves this repository, detects `skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md`, and installs the whole skill (`references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`) into every host root you select, including Cursor's: ```bash npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design ``` When the selected roots resolve to more than one skills directory, the CLI asks for an installation method and recommends **Symlink**: one canonical copy, linked into each root, so a later update reaches all of them at once. Pass `--copy` for independent copies per host instead. A selection that resolves to a single directory is copied, because the distinction is immaterial there. Where symlinks are unavailable (Windows without Developer Mode) the CLI falls back to copies and reports which roots it copied. This is a standalone install, separate from the marketplaces below: it does not follow marketplace updates automatically. Pull merged updates with `npx skills update diagram-design`. It also installs the Agent Skill only, so the `/export-diagram`, `/import-mermaid`, `/profile`, and `/doctor` command surfaces stay with the native packages. On a host that has one of the marketplaces below, prefer the marketplace. > **One-time migration:** an existing standalone `npx skills add` copy will not start following the Codex marketplace automatically. Remove that standalone copy, then use the Codex marketplace commands. Likewise, uninstall a personal Cowork copy and reinstall Diagram Design from your organization's marketplace. Future marketplace version bumps then flow through each client's native update path.
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design codex plugin add diagram-design@diagram-design ``` Codex refreshes configured Git marketplaces at startup. To fetch immediately, run `codex plugin marketplace upgrade diagram-design` and start a new session.
Qoder Clone the repository, validate the native plugin, and install it locally: ```bash git clone https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design.git qoder plugins validate ./diagram-design qoder plugins install ./diagram-design qoder plugins list ``` Qoder loads the canonical `skills/diagram-design/` tree and the shared command definitions directly; no Qoder-specific copy is maintained. For Qoder IDE, build a bounded ZIP from the tracked plugin surfaces and import it through **Extensions → Plugins → Add Plugins → Upload Plugin**: ```bash git -C diagram-design archive --format=zip \ --output=../diagram-design-qoder.zip HEAD \ .qoder-plugin commands skills LICENSE ``` Start a new task after installing or updating the plugin.
GitHub Copilot ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design copilot plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design ``` Copilot installs the shared Diagram Design skill plus its doctor, export, import, and profile capabilities from the existing repository marketplace. Confirm discovery with `copilot skill list` (or `/skills` in an interactive session), then ask for a diagram in natural language. To fetch a merged update, run `copilot plugin marketplace update diagram-design`, then `copilot plugin update diagram-design@diagram-design`.
Factory Droid ```bash droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design droid plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design --scope user ``` Droid tracks Git plugins by commit rather than the manifest's display version. To fetch a merged update, run `droid plugin marketplace update diagram-design`, then `droid plugin update diagram-design@diagram-design --scope user`, and start a new session.
Claude Cowork (organization marketplace) Organization GitHub marketplaces currently require a private or internal repository, so first mirror this public repository into one owned by your organization. In **Organization settings → Plugins**, choose **Add plugin → GitHub**, connect that mirror, and enable **Sync automatically** from the marketplace menu. Automatic sync runs when a pull request containing a plugin version bump is merged to the mirror's default branch; direct pushes do not trigger the webhook. Install Diagram Design from the resulting organization marketplace.
Pi ```bash pi install https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design ``` Run `/reload` in an open Pi session. Pi makes the skill available for matching diagram requests; use `/skill:diagram-design` to invoke it explicitly. Pi also loads the `/export-diagram`, `/import-mermaid`, `/import-excalidraw`, `/profile`, and `/doctor` prompt templates. The unpinned Git install is intentional: Pi has no automatic package refresh, so run `pi update --extensions` to pull merged updates.
Kiro Import the Agent Skill from the repository subdirectory URL: ```text https://github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design/tree/main/skills/diagram-design ``` Kiro copies imported skills into `.kiro/skills/` for a workspace or `~/.kiro/skills/` globally, so re-import the URL to pick up updates. Custom agents that declare resources should include `skill://diagram-design/**/SKILL.md`.
OpenCode Copy or symlink `skills/diagram-design/` to `.opencode/skills/diagram-design` in a project or `~/.config/opencode/skills/diagram-design` globally. OpenCode has no Diagram Design marketplace package; copied installs update only when you replace the directory from a newer checkout.
Editable install (customize the style guide in a clone) Managed installs are convenient, but changes to `references/style-guide.md` may be replaced by package updates. Saved profiles in `~/.diagram-design/profiles/` survive updates, and projects with a `.diagram-design` marker are unaffected. Clone the repo and install the local path if you plan to customize the working style guide directly: ```bash git clone git@github.com:cathrynlavery/diagram-design.git ~/code/diagram-design # Pi: register the checkout as a local package pi install ~/code/diagram-design # Claude Code: symlink the inner skill ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.claude/skills/diagram-design # Other Agent Skills hosts: create only the roots you use mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills ~/.cursor/skills ~/.cline/skills ~/.kiro/skills ~/.config/opencode/skills ~/.copilot/skills ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.agents/skills/diagram-design ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.cursor/skills/diagram-design ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.cline/skills/diagram-design ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.kiro/skills/diagram-design ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.config/opencode/skills/diagram-design ln -s ~/code/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design ~/.copilot/skills/diagram-design ``` The shared skill lives at `skills/diagram-design/`. Pi discovers it through the repo's standard `skills/` package directory; Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Factory Droid, Cursor, and other Agent Skills-compatible tools use the same files.
--- ## How it compares | | Mermaid / PlantUML | draw.io / Excalidraw | Diagram Design | |---|---|---|---| | You make it by | Writing text | Dragging shapes by hand | Describing it to your agent | | Layout | Automatic | Manual | Placed by the agent on a 4px grid, with CI checks for overlaps and clipping | | Look | The renderer's theme | Whatever you draw | One opinionated editorial style, matched to your brand | | Output | Text that renders on GitHub | An editable `.drawio` or `.excalidraw` file | One HTML file with inline SVG, exportable to SVG or PNG | | Change it later | Edit the text | Edit the canvas | Ask the agent again, or edit the SVG | | Existing diagrams | | | Redraws Mermaid, draw.io and Excalidraw files | The downsides are real. Output quality depends on the model you run it with, and the same prompt can lay out differently twice. The result is not an editable source format: there is no text to diff in a pull request and no canvas to drag a box on. For docs that live in Git and change every sprint, Mermaid is still the better fit. Diagram Design is for the diagram you are going to publish. --- ## Why I built it I wanted diagrams I actually liked for my blog posts on [littlemight.com](https://littlemight.com). Every time I needed one, whether an architecture sketch, a flowchart, or a pyramid of what matters most, I'd ask Claude and get back a generic rounded-box thing that looked nothing like the rest of the site. I'd either fight with Figma for 30 minutes or skip the diagram. The model already understood the content. What it was missing was taste, so I wrote the taste down: one accent color for the one or two things that matter, 1px hairlines, no shadows, every coordinate on a 4px grid. > *The highest-quality move is usually deletion.* Every node earns its place. The accent color is reserved for the 1 or 2 things the reader should look at first. Target density: 4/10. --- ## What it makes 45 diagram types, each in three static variants: minimal light, minimal dark, and full-editorial. Open any of them directly in a browser. There is no build step, JavaScript, or external image dependency.

Several types have named variants that share their reference: Line covers slopegraph, ridgeline, streamgraph and bump; Scatter covers bubble, beeswarm and box plot; Treemap covers marimekko. Architecture can nest administrative bands and traffic boxes in one snapshot when the hierarchy itself is the claim: dashed rx=4 bands for billing and permissions, solid rx=8 boxes for networks, and managed services outside every subnet. See the [containment example](skills/diagram-design/assets/example-architecture-containment.html) and [type-architecture.md](skills/diagram-design/references/type-architecture.md). See its [reference](skills/diagram-design/references/type-architecture-delta.md) and [order-fulfilment example](skills/diagram-design/assets/example-architecture-delta.html). ---
name: diagram-design
description: Create branded architecture, architecture delta, IT current-state, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER/data model, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, radar/spider, polar chart (polar/radial lollipop), loop/flywheel, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, exploded axonometric, axonometric plan, Venn, pyramid/funnel, treemap and marimekko, heatmap, bar and dumbbell, waterfall, line (slopegraph, ridgeline, streamgraph, bump), Gantt and scatter charts (bubble, beeswarm, box plot), high-level, process, medallion, data flow, DP integration, DP security matrix, Sankey, fishbone, Wardley map, kanban, user journey, service blueprint, deployment, dependency graph, UML class, story map, or database schema diagrams as HTML/SVG/PNG, with .drawio, Mermaid, and .excalidraw import, plus lifecycle phase maps, block decomposition trees, and onboarding guidance.

# Diagram Design

Create diagrams as self-contained HTML files with inline SVG and an editorial design system.

Forty-five visual types. Semantic patterns describe behavior; type references describe layout.

---

## 0. First-time setup — style guide gate

**Before generating your first diagram in a new project, verify the style guide has been customized.**

Do not silently ship default-skinned diagrams into a branded project.

First resolve any project `.diagram-design` marker per [`references/profiles.md`](references/profiles.md); a successfully resolved marker selects its profile and bypasses this gate. That reference owns failures, the protected default, and save behavior.

Open [`references/style-guide.md`](references/style-guide.md) and check the default tokens. If they are still the shipped defaults (paper `#f5f5f5`, ink `#2d3142`, accent `#bf4520`), **pause and ask the user**:

> *"This is your first diagram in this project and the style guide is still default. Customize now? Options: (a) website URL, (b) installed skill, (c) local folder/design-system, (d) paste tokens, (e) keep default, (f) load saved profile."*

Then branch per the matching section of [`references/onboarding.md`](references/onboarding.md); for **(f)** follow [`references/profiles.md`](references/profiles.md).

**Once the style guide has been customized** (or the user explicitly chose default), skip this gate on later runs. A leading profile header names the copied-in active profile. Without a header, any semantic-role value or typography family differing from shipped defaults means **custom-unsaved**: skip the gate and offer to save it as a profile. All-default tokens with no marker/header trigger the gate. After onboarding, offer to save as a named client profile per `references/profiles.md`.

---

## 1. Philosophy

**The highest-quality move is usually deletion.**

Applied to schematics:

- Every node represents a distinct idea. Two nodes that always travel together are one node.
- Every connection carries information. If the relationship is obvious from layout, remove the line.
- Coral is **editorial, not a flag.** 1–2 focal nodes per diagram. Using it on 5 nodes erases the signal.
- The schematic isn't done when everything is added. It's done when nothing can be removed.

**Target density: 4/10.** Enough to be technically complete. Not so dense it needs a guide. Above 9 nodes, it's probably two diagrams.

---

## 2. When to Use

Use for any of the 45 visual types (§3) when a reader will learn more from a visual than from prose, a table, or a bulleted list.

**Don't use for:**

- Quick unicode diagrams → a separate plain-text tool such as wiretext. This skill doesn't ship one.
- Lists of things → table or bullets.
- Attribute-only before/after → table; topology changes → Architecture delta.
- One-shape "diagrams" → just write the sentence.

Before drawing, ask: *Would the reader learn more from this than from a well-written paragraph?* If no, don't draw.

---

## 3. Selection: semantic pattern, then visual type

When behavior, state, enforcement, or risk carries the meaning, first load [`references/semantic-patterns.md`](references/semantic-patterns.md) and choose one primary pattern. Then choose the nearest visual type for layout. If no pattern matches, choose the type directly.

| Behavioral trigger | Semantic pattern → nearest type |
|---|---|
| Fan-in, queue depth, finite capacity, bottleneck | **Fan-in queue / bottleneck** → Data flow |
| Repeated Question / Input / Governance / Output slots across stages | **Stage framework with semantic slots** → Process |
| Conversation or loose input becomes a structured durable artifact | **Unstructured input → structured artifact** → Data flow |
| Two rule traces need pass/fail/skipped/not-reached and first divergence | **Paired policy-evaluation traces** → Flowchart |
| Trust boundaries plus permitted/forbidden ingress or deploy paths | **Secure paved road** → Architecture |
| Controls grouped by where they are enforced | **Governance / control catalog** → Layer stack |
| Defenses compensate for prior gaps and residual risk propagates | **Compensating security layers** → Layer stack |
| Hierarchical, ID-addressable decomposition needing per-block I/O, constraints, and a code link | **Traceable block decomposition** → Tree |
| One subject progresses through phases, waits, retries, cancellation, and terminal outcomes | **Lifecycle phase map** → State Machine |

The pattern owns semantic primitives and its tighter budget; the type owns layout grammar. Use [`references/animation.md`](references/animation.md) only when motion is requested or materially clarifies ordered change; static remains the default.

### Visual-type guide (45)

| If you're showing… | Use | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Components + connections in one snapshot; nested admin vs traffic scopes | **Architecture** | [type-architecture.md](references/type-architecture.md) |
| Structural change between synchronized Before / After topologies, with a Changes ledger | **Architecture delta** | [type-architecture-delta.md](references/type-architecture-delta.md) |
| Legacy IT landscape by phase or department; shows the *before* state | **IT current-state** | [type-it-state.md](references/type-it-state.md) |
| Decision logic with branches | **Flowchart** | [type-flowchart.md](references/type-flowchart.md) |
| Time-ordered messages between actors | **Sequence** | [type-sequence.md](references/type-sequence.md) |
| States + transitions + guards | **State machine** | [type-state.md](references/type-state.md) |
| Entities + fields + relationships | **ER / data model** | [type-er.md](references/type-er.md) |
| Events positioned in time | **Timeline** | [type-timeline.md](references/type-timeline.md) |
| Cross-functional process with handoffs | **Swimlane** | [type-swimlane.md](references/type-swimlane.md) |
| Two-axis positioning / prioritization | **Quadrant** | [type-quadrant.md](references/type-quadrant.md) |
| Multiple entities scored across 3–5 quantitative criteria | **Radar / Spider** | [type-radar.md](references/type-radar.md) |
| One quantitative series across cyclic categories; angle=category, radius=magnitude | **Polar chart** | [type-polar.md](references/type-polar.md) |
| Reinforcing cycle; the last step feeds the first and a hub accumulates state | **Loop** | [type-loop.md](references/type-loop.md) |
| Hierarchy through containment / scope | **Nested** | [type-nested.md](references/type-nested.md) |
| Parent → children relationships | **Tree** | [type-tree.md](references/type-tree.md) |
| Human/agent/team ownership, reporting, routing, escalation | **Org chart** | [type-org-chart.md](references/type-org-chart.md) |
| Stacked abstraction levels | **Layer stack** | [type-layers.md](references/type-layers.md) |
| Parts of one object pulled apart along one axis: a teardown, an unboxing, assembly order | **Exploded axonometric** | [type-exploded.md](references/type-exploded.md) |
| One floor or site seen from above at an angle: rooms with furniture, buildings by phase | **Axonometric plan** | [type-axonometric-plan.md](references/type-axonometric-plan.md) |
| Overlap between sets | **Venn** | [type-venn.md](references/type-venn.md) |
| Ranked hierarchy or conversion drop-off | **Pyramid / funnel** | [type-pyramid.md](references/type-pyramid.md) |
| Quantitative comparison across categories | **Bar chart** | [type-bar.md](references/type-bar.md) |
| A start total bridged to an end total by signed contributions (budget bridge, headcount deltas) | **Waterfall** | [type-waterfall.md](references/type-waterfall.md) |
| Part-of-whole where the relative sizes are the story | **Treemap** | [type-treemap.md](references/type-treemap.md) |
| Cross-tabulated data; fill encodes value per cell | **Heatmap** | [type-heatmap.md](references/type-heatmap.md) |
| Continuous trends over time, change between exactly two states (slopegraph), one distribution per series (ridgeline), or rank movement across several snapshots (bump) | **Line chart** | [type-line.md](references/type-line.md) |
| Tasks and phases on a timeline | **Gantt** | [type-gantt.md](references/type-gantt.md) |
| Correlation or distribution of two variables; bubble (three variables), beeswarm (one variable, dot per item), and box plot (five-number summary per group) variants | **Scatter plot** | [type-scatter.md](references/type-scatter.md) |
| End-to-end data stack on a container cluster | **High-Level** | [type-high-level.md](references/type-high-level.md) |
| Multi-actor sequential process with data handoffs | **Process** | [type-process.md](references/type-process.md) |
| Multi-tier data storage with quality levels and access policies | **Medallion** | [type-medallion.md](references/type-medallion.md) |
| Role-scoped data flow: who does what at each pipeline step | **Data flow** | [type-data-flow.md](references/type-data-flow.md) |
| Integration topology of a data platform — sources → core → consumers | **DP integration** | [type-dp-integration.md](references/type-dp-integration.md) |
| Per-role / per-component access permissions matrix | **DP security matrix** | [type-dp-security-matrix.md](references/type-dp-security-matrix.md) |
| A quantity splitting and merging across stages, band width = amount | **Sankey** | [type-sankey.md](references/type-sankey.md) |
| Causes of one observed effect, grouped by category (root-cause analysis) | **Fishbone** | [type-fishbone.md](references/type-fishbone.md) |
| Value chain against evolution — what to build, buy, and what is moving | **Wardley map** | [type-wardley.md](references/type-wardley.md) |
| Work-in-progress by state, with WIP limits and blocked items | **Kanban** | [type-kanban.md](references/type-kanban.md) |
| What a person does across stages of an experience, and how it feels | **User journey** | [type-journey.md](references/type-journey.md) |
| What the customer does vs what the service hides, across stages, with a line of visibility | **Service blueprint** | [type-service-blueprint.md](references/type-service-blueprint.md) |
| Where software runs — zones, hosts, artifacts, replicas, ports | **Deployment** | [type-deployment.md](references/type-deployment.md) |
| What depends on what, with fan-in and cycles a tree cannot express | **Dependency graph** | [type-dependency.md](references/type-dependency.md) |
| Classes with operations, inheritance, composition (other UML routes elsewhere) | **UML class** | [type-uml-class.md](references/type-uml-class.md) |
| Narrative backbone sliced into releases, with the cut line | **Story map** | [type-story-map.md](references/type-story-map.md) |
| Physical tables: SQL types, constraints, indexes, column-level FKs | **Database schema** | [type-db-schema.md](references/type-db-schema.md) |

Rules of thumb:

- If a 3-column table communicates the same thing, pick the table.
- If two types seem useful, pick the dominant axis; a semantic pattern may add behavior-specific primitives, not a second layout grammar.
- If you're past the compl

# text-to-cad The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks, generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal and CNC fabrication services. It is supported by all popular agents that support plugins or the [skills](https://skills.sh) framework, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Grok. ### How it works 1. Your agent writes each model as a Python script with [build123d](https://github.com/gumyr/build123d), built on [Open CASCADE](https://dev.opencascade.org). 2. Running the script, `python model.py`, builds the model with cadgen's engine into an `.xbf` document (its parts, names, colours, materials and joints) and the STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files the script declares. The engine keeps each model's work in memory, so an edit rebuilds only what it changed. 3. The CAD viewer shows the model in your agent app or your browser, and follows every rebuild. ## 🚀 Quickstart macOS and Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL https://texttocad.dev/install.sh | sh ``` Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://www.texttocad.dev/install.ps1 | iex ``` It installs uv if it is missing, then sets up text-to-cad in every agent app on your computer with each app's own commands (the plugin, which brings the skills and CAD's MCP server, or for an agent without a plugin the skills alone), registers the `cadgen` command, and stops an older release's engine that nothing is using. Run it again to update everything; it lists the apps to restart. Then ask your agent for a part or an assembly: it writes the model as a Python script, runs it to build the model and shows it in the CAD viewer. Installing by hand, app by app, and updates: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md) ## 🧰 Skills Install the library to give agents focused workflows for CAD, fabrication, robot description files, simulation, and local review. | Skill | Summary | Source | | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | CAD | Creates and edits CAD models from plain-language or image requests as Python scripts, built into XBF documents with STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB exports. | [skills/cad](skills/cad/SKILL.md) | | step.parts | Finds off-the-shelf STEP parts like screws, bearings, motors, and connectors. | [skills/step-parts](skills/step-parts/SKILL.md) | | Engineering Drawing | Dimensioned engineering drawings from a part, as a PDF: views, hidden lines, dimensions, hole callouts, title block. | [skills/engineering-drawing](skills/engineering-drawing/SKILL.md) | | DXF | Creates 2D DXF drawings like profiles, templates, gaskets, and cut layouts from Python sources or CAD geometry. | [skills/dxf](skills/dxf/SKILL.md) | | URDF | Writes robot structure files with links, joints, limits, inertials, and meshes. | [skills/urdf](skills/urdf/SKILL.md) | | SRDF | Adds MoveIt planning groups, end effectors, poses, and collision rules to a URDF. | [skills/srdf](skills/srdf/SKILL.md) | | SDF | Creates simulator models and worlds with frames, physics, sensors, and lights. | [skills/sdf](skills/sdf/SKILL.md) | | SendCutSend | Checks DXF and STEP files before upload to SendCutSend. | [skills/sendcutsend](skills/sendcutsend/SKILL.md) | | DfAM Check | Measures mesh printability per process: wall thickness, overhangs, support volume, and build orientation. | [skills/dfam-check](skills/dfam-check/SKILL.md) | | DFM | Reviews a part for sheet metal, CNC machining, or injection molding, with measured evidence and the cited rule behind every finding; measures draft, undercuts and projected area from a mesh. | [skills/dfm](skills/dfm/SKILL.md) | | G-code | Slices models into printer-ready G-code with OrcaSlicer, using your own printer presets. | [skills/gcode](skills/gcode/SKILL.md) | | Bambu Labs | Sends prints to Bambu Lab printers through Bambu Connect, Bambu Lab's official app, or Bambu Studio. | [skills/bambu-labs](skills/bambu-labs/SKILL.md) | ## 🛠️ Contributing text-to-cad is MIT-licensed and built in the open. - **Bugs and plugin requests**: [open an issue](https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad/issues/new). A bug report with the model script and the output of `cadgen doctor` is the fastest to fix, and an agent app without a plugin gets one on request. A security problem is reported privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says. - **Questions, ideas and what you made**: the [Discord](https://discord.gg/5FGB9DwJYU). By default, text-to-cad sends usage stats and crash reports, tagged with a random ID and never including your files, paths or prompts.
