---
name: cad
description: Creates and edits parametric CAD parts and assemblies as Python build123d models that cadgen's engine builds and the CAD Viewer shows live; exports STEP, STL, 3MF, GLB and xbf files on request; resolves prompt references, measures geometry, and articulates or animates assemblies. Use for 3D CAD modeling, editing a model script (any change to a part's or assembly's `.py`), organizing a CAD project, exporting or converting CAD files, Quick Edit prompts, mechanisms, and explode or showcase animations. Opens and reviews existing XBF, STEP/STP, STL, 3MF and GLB files in the CAD Viewer.
license: MIT
---

# CAD modeling and inspection

Provenance: maintained in [earthtojake/text-to-cad](https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad).
Use the installed local skill files for the current interface.

A model is a Python function; running its script rebuilds it in cadgen's warm engine, and the
page the person has open updates. Files are exports, made when asked.

## Start with the task

| Task | Start with | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Create or edit a part or assembly** | The project's model script, or a new one ([below](#write-a-model-and-run-it)). | [Models](references/model-contract.md), [build123d](references/build123d-modeling.md), [positioning](references/positioning.md) |
| **Organize a CAD project** | The project's existing layout. | [Project layout](references/project-layout.md) |
| **Export STEP, STL, 3MF, GLB or xbf** | `cadgen export <id> <file>`. | [Exports](references/exports.md) |
| **Use a vendor STEP, an xbf or a scan in a model** | `read_step`, `read_xbf` or `read_mesh` in the body. | [Inputs](references/model-contract.md#inputs) |
| **Resolve a reference from a prompt** | `cadgen inspect <id> '<ref>'`. | [References](references/inspection-and-validation.md#references) |
| **Measure or check geometry** | A check script that calls the model. | [Inspection](references/inspection-and-validation.md) |
| **See a model, a view or a pose** | `cadgen snapshot <id> out.png`. | [Snapshots](references/snapshot-review.md) |
| **Articulate a mechanism** | build123d joints in the body, then `cadgen.ap242`. | [Kinematics](references/kinematics.md) |
| **Explode, reveal or showcase a model** | `cadgen.gltf`'s `animation()` in the body. | [Animation](references/animation.md) |
| **Open an existing XBF, STEP/STP, STL, 3MF or GLB** | Show it to the user. | [Show the model](#show-the-model) |

A project built with cadgen 0.7 may need migrating: see [migrations](references/migrations.md).

For 2D DXF drawings use `$dxf`; this skill owns any 3D part the drawing projects.
Use the corresponding robot-description skill for URDF, SRDF or SDF.

## Setup and paths

Run cadgen through the `cadgen` command its installation writes, so this skill's commands
share one installation, and its engine server, with the CAD app's:

- `cadgen` below means `cadgen +0.8.4` (`~/.local/bin/cadgen +0.8.4` where `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH)
- `python` below means `cadgen +0.8.4 run`

For first-time setup or an update, a missing `cadgen` command, a release it says is not
installed, an engine that is not running, or an installation or kernel load error, read
[Setup and troubleshooting](references/setup.md).

One engine serves the installation: the first run starts it, every run and every
command goes through it, and it serves the viewer. `cadgen status` lists its workers
and the documents it holds; `cadgen stop` stops it, and any older one left running.
A build cut off by the shell's time limit keeps running in the engine; run the same
command again and it waits for that build and replays it (`cadgen status` shows it).
Give a cold build of a large model the shell tool's longest timeout, or run it in the
background. A command that ends with 'the system denies cadgen's local engine' is
another case: [Setup and troubleshooting](references/setup.md#diagnose-a-failure).

Command-line paths, and the paths `read_step`, `read_xbf`, `read_mesh` and `export`
take, are relative to the working directory, as are a model's own file reads. Anchor
them on `__file__` in code that must run from any folder.

## Write a model and run it

A part or an assembly is a function with no parameters, decorated `@model` (or with its
file decorators, never both), that returns a build123d shape. Its dimensions are the
arguments of a plain helper function, and each configuration is a `@model` of its own, with
its own id and page; constants several models share live in a module they import. A call
builds it and returns its document: a handle with `.id`, `.url`, `.shape` (the built shape)
and `.export(...)`. For example, `src/bracket.py`:

```python
import build123d as bd
from cadgen import model


def bracket_body(width, thickness, bore):
    body = bd.Box(width, 20, thickness)
    hole = bd.Cylinder(bore / 2, thickness)
    body = body - hole
    body.label = "bracket"
    body.color = "#4a6fa5"
    return body


@model
def bracket():
    return bracket_body(40, 6, 8)


@model
def bracket_wide():
    return bracket_body(60, 6, 8)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    bracket()
    bracket_wide()
```

```bash
python src/bracket.py
```

```text
built src/bracket.py::bracket cold in 2.61s: bodies 1 run; 6 misses, 0 hits; body 0.01s, names 0.00s, document 0.00s
  parts 1 · bounds 40 × 20 × 6 mm · joints 0 · sequences 0
  id: 0dc50a92-a21f-5895-a245-ebdeb5352f3b
  view: http://127.0.0.1:54360/0dc50a92-a21f-5895-a245-ebdeb5352f3b?token=...
built src/bracket.py::bracket_wide warm in 0.01s: bodies 1 run; 6 misses, 0 hits; body 0.01s, names 0.00s, document 0.00s
  parts 1 · bounds 60 × 20 × 6 mm · joints 0 · sequences 0
  id: 966d03a5-7b43-5bed-b75c-eb67d56c72d2
  view: http://127.0.0.1:54360/966d03a5-7b43-5bed-b75c-eb67d56c72d2?token=...
```

Each call the script's `__main__` makes prints how its model built, the delta under it
(parts, bounds, joints and sequences), its document's `id:` and its page, `view:` (the
handle's `.id` and `.url`). An unchanged rerun prints `took ... nothing ran` instead. Give the
user the page once ([Show the model](#show-the-model)) and use the id for every command
after it. The id comes from the
script's path and the function's name, or the script's folder and an explicit `@model(name="...")`,
so it is the same run after run, and the open page follows every run. A model's name is its identity
within its namespace, the function's name by default, `name=` gives it another. In 0.8 the namespace
is the script's folder; two explicit names in it must differ.

- **Running the script is the rebuild.** It writes no file. The engine's warm worker for
  the script replays every operation an edit did not reach, so a comment re-runs nothing
  and a dimension edit re-runs what reads it
  ([what a run runs](references/model-contract.md#what-a-run-runs)). Decoration only
  declares: keep the calls under `if __name__ == "__main__":` so other scripts can import
  the models.
- **`@memo` marks stages, never parts.** The engine already replays every kernel call, so
  mark only a function holding seconds of kernel work that an edit elsewhere leaves
  alone, such as a whole sub-assembly stage; never a part, never a helper called many
  times ([`@memo`](references/model-contract.md#memo-marks-stages)).
- **An assembly calls its parts.** Its body calls each part model and composes its shape
  (`plate().shape`), places and labels it, and returns a `Compound`. Each child builds in
  the same run and keeps its own document and id. Running a child's script alone leaves the assemblies that
  use it as they were: run the assembly.
- **`import build123d as bd`, and use it attribute-style** (`bd.Box`). The import is lazy:
  the kernel loads on first use, in the worker. `from build123d import Box`, or a
  module-level `bd.Color(...)` or `bd.Align` default, loads it at that line instead.
- **Colours are sRGB**, as a person picks them: `part.color = "#4a6fa5"`, or 0-255
  integers. Import `metals` from `bd_materials`; assign a native material with
  `part.material = metals.aluminum()`
  ([colour and materials](references/build123d-modeling.md#colour-and-materials)).
- **Inputs** are `read_step`, `read_xbf` and `read_mesh` in the body, and any file its
  Python opens, each tracked by its bytes. The clock, environment variables and
  randomness are not seen: a body is a function of its code and its inputs. Compose
  project models by calling them, never by reading a file the project exported.
- **References** to faces, edges and parts come from `cadgen inspect <id> [ref]`, and the
  body picks the same element with build123d's selectors; verify with a snapshot when in
  doubt ([references](references/inspection-and-validation.md#references)).
- **A shape with no function** (a notebook cell, a REPL) is handed over:
  `model(shape, name="plate")` returns the same handle, and no command builds it again.
- **The engine never reruns code.** A restart reopens every document from the engine's
  cache, as last built. When the cache holds no file of one (deleted by hand, or never
  saved), the page, `cadgen inspect <id>` and `cad_show` print the command that brings it
  back (`cadgen run src/bracket.py`). Run it.
- Model units are millimetres, +Z up. `$step-parts` finds real vendor models of
  purchasable parts such as fasteners, bearings and servos.
- An image without a scale sets no fit dimension, and a drawing's units, projection and
  revision decide how its numbers read. A missing or conflicting dimension that changes
  the result is the person's to settle; a value chosen in its place is an assumption.

## Files, when asked

A file is an action on the document the engine holds, never part of the model: no code
change and no rebuild, written at once. It holds what the document held when it was
written, so a change made after it is in the file only once it is written again. Write one
when the person asks for it:

```bash
cadgen export "$ID" STEP/bracket.step STL/bracket.stl GLB/bracket.glb 3MF/bracket.3mf
```

A project with standing deliverables gets an `exports.py` that imports its models and
calls `export(x, path, ...)` on each (`x` a model call's handle); running it rewrites every deliverable
([exports](references/exports.md)). An export takes a document and its destinations,
and nothing else: a posed file is a model that returns the posed assembly
(`posed(arm(), "folded")`), and a part on its own is the part's own model.

The xbf, cadgen's own document, is Save As: export one only to share a model without its
code, or to compose it in another project with `read_xbf`. A restart needs none: the
engine's own cache reopens every document it built, as last built. A vendor STEP is
converted to an xbf once
(`cadgen export vendor/motor.step vendor/motor.xbf`) and read with `read_xbf`, many
times faster than parsing the STEP.

## Projects built around exported files

A project can instead revolve around its exported files, but only when the person asks to
iterate on the exported file itself or the project already does: an `exports.py`, a consumer
that reads the files (a robot description, a slicer, a drawing pipeline), or a 0.7-era
layout, whose runs wrote files. The loop is three steps. The script writes the file on each
run, by a file decorator in place of `@model` (`@step("../STEP/bracket.step")`, relative to
the script), or `exports.py` or `cadgen export` follows the run. Show the file's page, not
the model's: it follows the file on disk, updating when a run rewrites the file.
Verification reads the file: `cadgen snapshot` or `cadgen inspect` with its path, or
`read_step` in a check. The costs keep the default the default: each iteration pays the
file's translation and the page's re-read, a STEP parsed again; a file names no model, so a
ref picked on its page has no `made_by` and a Quick Edit from it no way back into the code;
and the model's page stays the better place to look while editing.

resources.readme_excerpt:
VoiceStudio

AI voice studio. On your device.

Clone, design, dub, dictate, transcribe and narrate in 646 languages.

Runs on your laptop, desktop, servers, phone, tablets and more

Website · Download · Get started · Docs · Discord · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский

Strategic sponsors

Special sponsor


Demo workspace · Default dark theme · Watch the HD tour

## What you can do

Voice cloning
Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice.
Video dubbing
Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original.

Voice design
Describe a voice in words and generate it.
Local models
Choose your engines and download only the models you need.
More screenshots

Workspace overview
Model packs
- **Dictate & transcribe** — A floating dictation widget and local transcription - **Narrate & batch** — Stories, audiobooks and queued jobs - **Connect & automate** — Local API, MCP, reusable recipes and watch folders Start with **VoiceStudio** (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or pick from dozens of other engines in the Model Manager. See the [features & engine catalog](docs/feature-catalog.md). ## Platforms | Platform & status | Downloads & acceleration | | :--- | :--- | |  **macOS** (Apple Silicon)
Stable | `.dmg` · [guide](docs/install/macos.md)
Metal (MPS) | |  **Windows 10/11** (x64)
Stable | `.exe` · [guide](docs/install/windows.md)
NVIDIA CUDA · [AMD ROCm (opt-in)](docs/install/windows-rocm.md) · CPU | |  **Linux** (x64)
Stable | `.AppImage` · `.deb` · · [Nix](docs/install/nix.md) · [guide](docs/install/linux.md)
NVIDIA CUDA · CPU | |  **Docker**
Stable | [GHCR](docs/install/docker.md "ghcr.io/debpalash/voicestudio")
NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm | |  **Android** 10+
Preview | `.apk` · [guide](docs/mobile.md#install)
On-device, offline | |  **iPhone / iPad** (iOS 17+)
Preview | `.ipa` (sideload) · [guide](docs/mobile.md#install)
On-device, offline | |  **Windows on ARM**
Experimental | `.exe` · [guide](docs/install/windows.md)
CPU (x64 backend under emulation) | |  **Intel Mac**
Limited | `.dmg` · [why](docs/install/macos.md)
App UI only, connects to a remote backend | Desktop and phone installers are on the [latest release](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest); Docker images come from GHCR. No GPU? The app is fully usable on the CPU, just slower. Native GGUF engines can also use Vulkan on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs; OmniVoice GGUF picks its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux ([OmniVoice](docs/engines/omnivoice-gguf.md#vulkan-acceleration), [CosyVoice](docs/engines/cosyvoice-gguf.md)). Speed by engine and hardware: [performance](docs/performance.md). ## Get started **macOS / Linux** ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ``` **Windows** (PowerShell) ```powershell irm https://voicestudio.sh/install.ps1 | iex ``` Or download an installer from the table above. Then open **Voice cloning**, pick a voice or add a clean reference recording, type your text and generate. The app asks before it downloads any model. > [!NOTE] > On macOS, "VoiceStudio is damaged and can't be opened" means Gatekeeper blocked the app, not that the download is broken. See the [Gatekeeper fix](docs/install/macos.md#gatekeeper-quarantine).
More install options: a specific version, current main, uninstall, from source, with a coding agent ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z # a specific release curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --main # build current main curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --uninstall # remove the app, keep your data ``` If `voicestudio.sh` is unreachable, run the script straight from the repository: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`. Prerequisites and behavior: [installer guide](docs/install/script.md). **From source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git cd VoiceStudio bun run dev ``` `bun run dev` installs the JavaScript dependencies and, when using a supported local backend, the Python dependencies before launching Electron. Run `bun run setup:api` directly when you only need to rebuild the Python environment. See [Electron setup](electron/README.md). **With a coding agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …), paste: ```text Install the VoiceStudio app on this device and verify it works, following https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/blob/main/docs/install/agent.md ``` Upgrading from 0.5.3 or older (the Tauri app)? [Install the new app separately](docs/electron-migration.md).
## Documentation | Need | Start here | |---|---| | Setup help | [Troubleshooting](docs/install/troubleshooting.md) · [Model downloads](docs/downloading-models.md) | | Guides | [Multi-speaker dubbing](docs/dubbing/multi-speaker-guide.md) · [Expressive speech](docs/expressive-speech.md) · [Exporting dubs](docs/dubbing/export.md) | | Models & quality | [Engine guides](docs/engines/README.md) · [whisper.cpp ASR](docs/engines/whisper-cpp.md) · [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md) | | Integrations | [Local API](docs/speech-platform.md) · [MCP](docs/mcp.md) · [Examples](examples/README.md) | | Phone apps | [iOS and Android](docs/mobile.md) | | Development | [Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) ([sign the CLA](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-licensing) before your first PR) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Agent skills: `npx skills add debpalash/VoiceStudio` (**voicestudio** for audio work, **voicestudio-maintainer** for the repo). ## Sponsors VoiceStudio is free and has no paid cloud behind it. Sponsors keep it shipping: they fund maintainer time, test hardware, code-signing and release infrastructure.

For sponsorship inquiries, contact [sponsor@voicestudio.sh](mailto:sponsor@voicestudio.sh). [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/debpalash) · [PayPal](https://paypal.me/palashCoder) · [Tiers and benefits](SPONSORS.md) · [Get your logo listed](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/issues/new?template=sponsor.yml) ## Other projects More open-source tools from the people building VoiceStudio. - **[OpenGTM](https://opengtm.palash.dev/?utm_source=voicestudio&utm_medium=sponsor&utm_campaign=strategic-sponsor&utm_content=related-projects)** — Find and enrich companies and people in a self-hosted go-to-market workspace. [Source](https://github.com/debpalash/OpenGTM). - **[Opal](https://opal.palash.dev/?utm_source=voicestudio&utm_medium=sponsor&utm_campaign=strategic-sponsor&utm_content=related-projects)** — Watch, stream and browse your media in one native, open-source player. [Source](https://github.com/debpalash/Opal). - **[Supermetry](https://supermetry.com/?utm_source=voicestudio&utm_medium=sponsor&utm_campaign=strategic-sponsor&utm_content=related-projects)** — Understand your websites and products with self-hosted, cookie-free analytics. [Source](https://github.com/velixio/supermetry). More projects: [debpalash](https://github.com/debpalash?tab=repositories) · [velixio](https://github.com/velixio?tab=repositories) ## Team ### Core team

Palash Debnath
Creator and Core Team
palash.dev · GitHub · X
Shimul Debnath
Core Team
shimul.me · GitHub · X
### Contributors Thank you to everyone who sends code, reports, translations and ideas. [All contributors](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/graphs/contributors) · [Contribute](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) ## License & responsible use [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE) covers the app, including commercial use under its terms. Model weights, voices and generated output have their own licences, which the Model Manager shows for each model ([inventory](docs/licensing/model-inventory.md)).   "name": "omnivoice-studio-monorepo",

  "packageManager": "bun@1.4.2",
  "scripts": {
    "setup:api": "node scripts/setup-api.mjs",

    "dev:frontend": "bun run --cwd electron dev:web",
    "dev:desktop": "bun run --cwd electron dev",
    "wait:api": "node scripts/wait-app-port.mjs api",
    "wait:frontend": "node scripts/wait-app-port.mjs web",
    "predev": "node scripts/prepare-dev.mjs",
    "dev": "bun run --cwd electron dev",
    "predesktop": "bun install",
    "desktop": "bun run --cwd electron dev",
    "build": "bun run --cwd electron build",
    "check:electron": "node scripts/validate_store_foundation.mjs && bun run --cwd electron typecheck && bun run --cwd electron test && bun run --cwd electron build && bun run --cwd electron build:web && node electron/tests/packaging-contract.mjs",
    "start": "bun run --cwd electron start",

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "omnivoice"
version = "0.5.7"
description = "VoiceStudio — a private, local-first studio for voice cloning, speech generation, dubbing, transcription, and audiobooks"
readme = "README.md"
# Free and open-source under the GNU Affero General Public License v3 (see
# LICENSE). A commercial license is available for proprietary/closed-source use
# without AGPL obligations — contact hi@voicestudio.sh. The bundled omnivoice/
# TTS model by Han Zhu remains Apache-2.0 upstream (Apache-2.0 is AGPL-compatible).
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [{name = "Debpalash"}, {name = "Han Zhu"}]
keywords = [
    "tts",
    "text-to-speech",
    "speech-synthesis",
    "zero-shot",
    "multilingual",
    "diffusion",
    "voice-cloning",
]
classifiers = [
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",

    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Multimedia :: Sound/Audio :: Speech",

    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
]
dependencies = [
    "torch>=2.4",
    "torchaudio>=2.4",
    "torchvision>=0.19",
    "transformers>=5.10.0",
    "accelerate",
    "pydub",
    "gradio>=6.15.1",
    "tensorboardX",
    "webdataset",
    "numpy",
    "soundfile",
    # whisperx / faster-whisper import `pkg_resources` at runtime. setuptools
    # 80+ DROPPED the bundled pkg_resources, so an unpinned ">=75" now resolves
    # to a version WITHOUT it → "No module named 'pkg_resources'", which both
    # breaks WhisperX transcription and makes its is_available() report false
    # ("No ASR backend is ready"). Cap below 80 so pkg_resources stays present
    # (issue #224; also #58). Revisit when whisperx/faster-whisper drop the
    # pkg_resources dependency.
    "setuptools>=75,<80",
    "psutil>=7.2.2",
    # Pinned to 3.x — pyannote 4.x removed `use_auth_token` from `Inference`
    # which whisperx 3.4.2 still passes, blowing up `whisperx.load_model()`
    # with TypeError. whisperx tests against pyannote 3.3.2+, so we track
    # that range and revisit when whisperx releases a 4-compatible build.
    "pyannote-audio>=3.3.2,<4.0",
    "imageio-ffmpeg>=0.6.0",
    # Directly used by video_context; 12.1 adds get_flattened_data(), the
    # replacement for getdata() ahead of its Pillow 14 removal.
    "pillow>=12.1.0",
    # Effects-chain API needs 0.9.14+. Linux x86_64 wheels from 0.9.21 are
    # built with -march=native (upstream spotify/pedalboard#454), so
    # `import pedalboard` dies with SIGILL on CPUs lacking the builder's SIMD
    # set (#2052). 0.9.20 is the last good wheel; revisit once upstream ships
    # portable builds.
    "pedalboard>=0.9.14,<0.9.21",
    # Primary ASR — cross-platform, CTranslate2-based under the hood. WhisperX
    # adds wav2vec2 forced alignment (±10-30 ms word timing vs Whisper's own
    # ±100-300 ms) which directly improves lip-sync on the dub pipeline.
    # Pulls `faster-whisper` transitively, so a WhisperX install also provides
    # the plain faster-whisper backend as a fallback for rare-language audio
    # where no wav2vec2 alignment model exists.
    "whisperx>=3.1.0",
    "faster-whisper>=1.0.0",
    # Apple Silicon-only speedup; skipped everywhere else so `uv sync` can
    # succeed on Linux/Windows/mac-Intel (no mlx wheels exist for those).
    "mlx-whisper>=0.2.1 ; sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'",
    # Apple Silicon-only rich TTS library — 14+ engines (Kokoro, CSM, Dia,
    # Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox, MeloTTS, OuteTTS, Spark, Higgs-Audio, Voxtral,
    # …). Gives mac-ARM users a broad engine picker in Settings. Also gated
    # by platform markers because it depends on mlx (Apple Silicon only).
    "mlx-audio>=0.4.4 ; sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'",
    # Apple Silicon-only Parakeet TDT v3 ASR (mlx-community/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    # via MLX). Gives mac-ARM the Parakeet tier CUDA/CPU users get from
    # sherpa/NeMo: 25 European languages, TDT token/word timestamps, ~2 GB
    # unified memory, dictation-grade speed on the GPU. Same platform gate as
    # mlx-whisper/mlx-audio (depends on mlx — no wheels elsewhere).
    "parakeet-mlx>=0.5.2 ; sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'",
    "demucs>=4.0.1",
    "yt-dlp>=2026.7.4",
    # >=1.16: alembic.ini relies on path_separator=os (new in 1.16.0), which
    # older alembic silently ignores and then colon-splits C:\ paths /
    # space-splits POSIX paths containing spaces.
    "alembic>=1.16",
    # Lightweight English TTS "Turbo" tier — 25-80 MB ONNX model, 8 preset
    # voices (Bella, Jasper, Luna, Bruno, Rosie, Hugo, Kiki, Leo), CPU
    # realtime on any platform. Complements OmniVoice's 2.4 GB multilingual
    # zero-shot clone: when the caller just needs fast English narration with
    # no reference sample, this is ~100× smaller + ~10× faster. Pinned to
    # the exact wheel because the project is in developer preview and the
    # 0.x API is explicitly unstable.
    "kittentts @ https://github.com/KittenML/KittenTTS/releases/download/0.8.1/kittentts-0.8.1-py3-none-any.whl",
    # Invisible audio watermarking — embeds imperceptible neural watermarks
    # in AI-generated speech for provenance detection (SynthID-like).
    # MIT license, ~5ms per segment on CPU, 16-bit message payload.
    "audioseal>=0.1.3",
    # API server — always needed for the Studio UI.
    # 0.137 makes included routers lazy `_IncludedRouter` entries, breaking
    # route-table consumers that require the concrete HTTP/WebSocket routes.
    "fastapi<0.137",
    "scalar-fastapi",
    "uvicorn",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.31",
    # Required by uvicorn for WebSocket support (real-time sidebar events).
    "websockets",
    # Offline translation — listed as builtin in the engine registry so the
    # "Argos (Local, Fast)" option in the Dub tab works out-of-the-box.
    "argostranslate>=1.9.0",
    # Phase 1 AUTH-02: Fernet symmetric encryption + scrypt KDF for the
    # at-rest HF token in the SQLite settings store. Pulled in directly so
    # we don't depend on a transitive arrival via pyannote/huggingface_hub
    # (Assumption A1 in RESEARCH.md was checked at execute-time and proved
    # false — `cryptography` is not on the install path today).
    "cryptography>=41",
    "mcp>=1.28.1,<2",
    # Opt-in product analytics (core/analytics.py). Inert unless the build ships a
    # POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN *and* the user opts in — default OFF. No exception
    # autocapture (it would ship raw tracebacks past core.failure.sanitize()).
    "posthog>=3.7",
    # Fast model downloads (FDL plan). huggingface_hub arrives transitively via
    # transformers, but we pin it directly so the Xet fast-download path can't
    # silently disappear on a resolve, and we pull `hf-xet` explicitly: it is
    # the content-defined-chunking, parallel byte-range downloader that gives
    # IDM/uGet-style speed for Xet-backed repos (the entire current model
    # catalog — FDL spike 2026-06-13; plan removed with .planning/, see git history).
    # hf-xet is 64-bit only (fine for every OmniVoice target). Do NOT add
    # `hf_transfer` — it is deprecated in favour of Xet and breaks progress
    # callbacks (the accurate-progress work in this same plan depends on tqdm).
    "huggingface_hub>=1.7",
    "hf-xet>=1.1",
    # Audiobook PDF ingest (/audiobook/import). Pure-Python, MIT, zero native
    # deps → identical behaviour on macOS/Windows/Linux (default-parity rule).
    # EPUB + plaintext stay stdlib-only; only PDF needs a real parser, and
    # pypdf is the lightest one that ships no C extensions.
    "pypdf>=6.19.0",
    # LLM client for Cinematic dub refinement, glossary auto-extract, and
    # LLM-based translation (services.llm_backend / translator / dub_translate
    # all `from openai import OpenAI`). Talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint —
    # OpenAI, Ollama (http://localhost:11434/v1), LM Studio, vLLM — so it's the
    # local-first path too (no key, nothing leaves the machine). Pure-Python, no
    # native deps → identical on macOS/Windows/Linux. Previously undeclared, so
    # `uv sync` never installed it and Cinematic was dead-on-arrival on every
    # source install ("Cinematic needs an LLM" even with Ollama running, because
    # is_available() returned "openai package missing"); the UI's `pip install
    # openai` hint landed in the wrong interpreter on a managed venv.
    "openai>=1.40",
    # Native paid-provider protocols behind the same LLM feature interface.
    "litellm>=1.103.0,<2",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "boto3>=1.40",
    "google-auth>=2.29,<3",
    # sherpa-onnx live-dictation ASR engine (CPU, cross-platform). The thin
    # `sherpa-onnx` wheel declares `sherpa-onnx-core` only in its *wheel*
    # metadata (not the sdist), so uv's resolver does NOT pull it transitively
    # — without core, `import sherpa_onnx` fails at load time (missing
    # libonnxruntime). Pin core EXPLICITLY so the lock captures it and Docker's
    # frozen `uv sync` installs a working engine on every platform.
    "sherpa-onnx>=1.13.3",
    "sherpa-onnx-core>=1.13.3",
    # SOCKS proxy support for httpx (#959). huggingface_hub's get_session()
    # builds an httpx.Client, which raises ImportError AT CONSTRUCTION when
    # ALL_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY is socks5:// and socksio isn't importable — every
    # model load/download 500'd for SOCKS-proxy users ("Using SOCKS proxy, but
    # the 'socksio' package is not installed"). Same failure shape for the
    # OpenAI SDK's client. Pure-Python, MIT, zero transitive deps, ~13 KB —
    # identical on macOS/Windows/Linux.
    "socksio>=1.0",
    # OS trust store for TLS (#976). Users behind a corporate/antivirus proxy
    # that TLS-inspects traffic get a raw "[SSL: SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE]"
    # on every model install — the TCP connection succeeds, but the proxy's
    # re-signed certificate is trusted by the OS (Windows CryptoAPI/SChannel)
    # and not by Python's bundled `certifi` CA list. `truststore` patches
    # `ssl.SSLContext` to verify against the OS trust store instead. Pure-
    # Python, MIT, PyPA-maintained, zero transitive deps — same class of fix
    # as socksio above, identical on macOS/Windows/Linux.
    "truststore>=0.9",
    # Numbers→words for the pre-TTS text normalization pass
    # (services/text_normalization.py). Was already installed transitively;
    # promoted to a direct dependency because we now import it ourselves.
    "num2words>=0.5.14",
    "pip>=26.1.2",
    # Direct URL (not [tool.uv.sources]) so EVERY installer sees it — Docker's
    # `uv pip install --system .` reads only project metadata and would try to
    # resolve a bare name from PyPI, where spaCy models don't exist. Same form
    # as kittentts above.
    "en-core-web-sm @ https://github.com/explosion/spacy-models/releases/download/en_core_web_sm-3.8.0/en_core_web_sm-3.8.0-py3-none-any.whl",
    # Security floors for pyannote-audio's checkpoint loader (GHSA-qqmf-gpg7-g8gw).
    # Declared here, not only in uv.lock, so `uv pip install .` (Docker, Colab)
    # cannot keep a preinstalled 2.6.5 that pyannote's `lightning>=2.0.1` allows.
    "lightning>=2.6.6",
    "pytorch-lightning>=2.6.6",
    "nvidia-ml-py>=13.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]

eval = [
    "jiwer==3.1.0",       # WER
    "librosa",             # Audio processing
    "s3prl",               # Speech representation (HuBERT etc.)
    "funasr",              # ASR models
    "zhconv",              # Chinese character normalization
    "zhon",                # Chinese punctuation
    "unidecode",            # Unicode normalization
]
ui = [
    "gradio>=6.15.1",
    "gradio_client",
    "requests",
]
# Phase 3 Plan 03-01 — Supertonic-3 opt-in engine. CPU-only ONNX TTS,
# 31 languages, ~99M params, ~400 MB model on first use. Default
# `uv sync --no-dev` does NOT install this; users opt in with
# `uv sync --extra supertonic` after accepting the OpenRAIL-M model
# license in Settings → Engines.
#
# Publisher verified per Plan 03-01 Task 1 (Package Legitimacy Audit):
#   • PyPI maintainers = Yu Yechan / Juheon Lee / Hyeongju Kim (Supertone Inc.)
#   • Repository = github.com/supertone-inc/supertonic-py
#   • Same publisher ships supertonic-js on npm (same maintainer email)

]
# PocketTTS opt-in engine. Keep the SDK pinned: its model-loading and voice

    # pocket-tts requires torch>=2.5; PyTorch no longer publishes macOS x86_64
    # wheels at those versions. Keep the opt-in extra installable everywhere,
    # with an explicit engine availability reason on Intel Macs.
    "pocket-tts==2.1.0 ; sys_platform != 'darwin' or platform_machine != 'x86_64'",
]

import importlib
import os
import sys

# Ensure `backend/` is on sys.path so bare imports like `from core.config`
# work regardless of how uvicorn is invoked:
#   - `uvicorn main:app`           (cwd = backend/)
#   - `uvicorn backend.main:app`   (cwd = /app, Docker)
_backend_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if _backend_dir not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _backend_dir)

from core.crash_diagnostics import enable_fault_handler  # noqa: E402
from core.app_config import PRODUCT_NAME  # noqa: E402
# Arm native-crash tracebacks before model or GPU libraries can be imported.
enable_fault_handler()
# PyInstaller re-executes this entry module when the frozen backend binary is
# launched. Nested operation supervisors therefore dispatch here, before math,
# logging, FastAPI, torch, or any application initialization. Source launches
# use this same entry contract so frozen/source behavior cannot drift.
if __name__ == "__main__" and len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "--supervise":
    from core.contained_subprocess import supervisor_main

    raise SystemExit(supervisor_main(sys.argv[1:]))

# Rust clears CLOEXEC only for the backend exec. Re-arm PEP 446 immediately:
# nested supervisors receive this descriptor solely through explicit pass_fds,
# so a third-party close_fds=False child cannot hold the desktop drain barrier.
from core.contained_subprocess import secure_backend_drain_fd  # noqa: E402

secure_backend_drain_fd()

# The shell reads our stdout/stderr through pipes; a reader that falls behind
# would otherwise block uvicorn's access-log write on the event loop and freeze
# /health (#2970 class). Producers get a bounded buffer instead.
from core.nonblocking_stdio import install as _install_nonblocking_stdio  # noqa: E402

_install_nonblocking_stdio()

import math  # noqa: E402

# Windows: run every child process (ffmpeg, engine sidecars, yt-dlp, demucs, …)
# WITHOUT popping a console window. The backend itself is spawned console-less by
# the Tauri shell, so on Windows each console subprocess it launches would
# otherwise get a brand-new cmd window flashed on screen. Patch subprocess.Popen
# once, before anything spawns, so our 70+ call sites AND third-party libraries
# (imageio-ffmpeg, yt-dlp) are all covered. No-op off Windows. (#1178)
from core.win_subprocess import install as _install_no_window  # noqa: E402

_install_no_window()

# Windows (#2276): one client resetting its connection mid-accept (WinError 64
# etc., typical of AV/VPN loopback inspection) makes asyncio's ProactorEventLoop
# close the LISTENING socket, so the backend lives on but never answers again.
# Re-arm accept on transient errors instead. Class-level patch, so it covers
# every launch path (`python main.py`, the Electron `uvicorn main:app` CLI
# which imports this module before binding) and every server on the loop.
# No-op off Windows. See core/win_accept_guard.py.
from core.win_accept_guard import install as _install_accept_guard  # noqa: E402

_install_accept_guard()

# #564: also make the project's OWN `omnivoice` package importable from source
# when the venv's editable install is missing/broken (interrupted/offline
# `uv sync`, antivirus-quarantined `_editable_impl_omnivoice.pth`, …). Without
# this the backend boots fine and only fails at the first model call with
# `No module named 'omnivoice'`. The bootstrap now gates on omnivoice being
# importable too (re-syncing to re-lay the editable install); this is the
# runtime safety net. See core/omnivoice_path.py for the full rationale.
from core.omnivoice_path import ensure_omnivoice_importable
ensure_omnivoice_importable(_backend_dir)

# Windows builds have no Triton, so torch compilation would fail only when
# inference begins. Set the opt-outs before model_manager can import torch,
# while preserving any values the user already supplied.
if sys.platform == "win32":
    for _compile_opt_out in (
        "TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE",
        "TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE",
        "TORCHINDUCTOR_DISABLE",
    ):
        os.environ.setdefault(_compile_opt_out, "1")

# The Intel Fortran runtime bundled with MKL (under numpy/scipy) installs a
# console CTRL handler that aborts the whole process with `forrtl: error
# (200): program aborting due to window-CLOSE event` when a Windows console
# CLOSE/LOGOFF/SHUTDOWN event reaches it — seen in the wild as backend crashes
# with exit code 2 / 0xC000013A mid-session (#1153 class). The RTL reads this
# at DLL init, so it must be set before torch/numpy import MKL; setdefault so
# an explicit user value wins. A no-op everywhere the Fortran RTL isn't
# handling console events (macOS/Linux), hence unconditional (and testable).
os.environ.setdefault("FOR_DISABLE_CONSOLE_CTRL_HANDLER", "1")

# The backend's stdout/stderr are pipes owned by the desktop shell that
# spawned it. If that shell exits while the backend survives (crash,
# relaunch, orphan), the pipes close — and the next write raises
# BrokenPipeError. transformers' tqdm weight-loading bar writes constantly,
# so an orphaned backend couldn't load the model at all (caught in the wild
# by the in-app diagnostic report). Wrap stdio so EPIPE is swallowed
# process-wide: logs are best-effort for a server, model loading is not.
# (utils.hf_progress.SafeFileWrapper — same wrapper the patched hub tqdm
# already uses for its own fp.)
from utils.hf_progress import SafeFileWrapper as _SafeStdio  # noqa: E402
from core.parent_liveness import arm_desktop_parent_watchdog  # noqa: E402

# Force UTF-8 stdio before wrapping (#1155): on Windows the spawned backend's
# stdout defaults to cp1252, and any library that prints user text (kittentts
# prints the full synth text on every generate) raised UnicodeEncodeError on
# Vietnamese/CJK/…, killing the request with a bogus 400. backslashreplace
# keeps even a non-UTF-8-able sink from ever raising.
for _stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
    try:
        _stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="backslashreplace")
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — pythonw/frozen builds may lack reconfigure
        pass

# The desktop keeps the backend's stdin pipe open for its own lifetime. EOF is
# therefore a stable ownership signal that survives PID reuse and lets a child
# terminate even when the shell crashes before its normal process-tree teardown.
arm_desktop_parent_watchdog()

if not getattr(sys.stdout, "_is_safe_wrapper", False):
    sys.stdout = _SafeStdio(sys.stdout)
if not getattr(sys.stderr, "_is_safe_wrapper", False):
    sys.stderr = _SafeStdio(sys.stderr)

try:
    import dotenv

    _discovered_env = dotenv.find_dotenv()
    # Also load .env from the project root (parent of backend/)
    _project_env = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(_backend_dir), ".env")
    from core.env_startup import load_startup_env as _load_startup_env
    # Load the durable per-user config (the in-app Settings source of truth) so
    # env vars set once survive Tauri/Finder launches that don't inherit a shell
    # environment. This OVERRIDES launcher-injected defaults: the desktop app
    # injects a stale OMNIVOICE_CACHE_DIR from its own config before startup, so
    # without override a models dir changed in Settings was ignored forever (#480).
    _load_startup_env(_discovered_env, _project_env)
except ImportError:
    pass

# A mirror in HF_ENDPOINT must never receive the Hugging Face token, here or in
# engine processes that inherit this environment.
from services.hf_auth import apply_process_token_policy as _apply_hf_token_policy  # noqa: E402

_apply_hf_token_policy()

# Importing it removes Electron's account-bridge capability from os.environ, so
# engine and tool subprocesses never inherit it.
importlib.import_module("services.cloud_account")

# ── cuDNN 8 library preload ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Moved into _phase_a_build (`native_preload` step, early-bind refactor): the
# native dlopen/LoadLibrary belongs to the deferred heavy phase, and its one
# hard invariant — run before any ctranslate2/torch import — is preserved
# there (native_preload strictly precedes ml_imports).

# Route HF/Torch caches to a single external directory when requested.
_cache_dir = os.environ.get("OMNIVOICE_CACHE_DIR")
if _cache_dir:
    os.makedirs(_cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ["HF_HOME"] = _cache_dir
    os.environ["HF_HUB_CACHE"] = _cache_dir
    os.environ["TORCH_HOME"] = _cache_dir

# ── Windows symlink fix ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# HuggingFace Hub creates NTFS symlinks in its cache to deduplicate blobs
# across model revisions.  On Windows, symlink creation requires either
# Developer Mode enabled or an elevated (Administrator) shell.  Without
# either, `snapshot_download` / `hf_hub_download` raises:
#   OSError: [WinError 1314] A required privilege is not held by the client
# Setting HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS_WARNING silences the console spam, and the
# newer HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS (huggingface_hub ≥ 0.21) forces file copies
# instead — slightly more disk but always works on first install.
if sys.platform == "win32":
    os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS_WARNING", "1")
    os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS", "1")

# ── HF Xet → legacy LFS fallback ────────────────────────────────────────────
# huggingface_hub ≥ 1.5 routes large file downloads through the Xet content-
# addressed protocol (hf_xet runtime), which has its own internal progress
# reporting that bypasses our `tqdm` monkey-patch in `utils.hf_progress`.
# As a result the SetupWizard install rows show no byte progress while the
# download is actually running. Force the legacy LFS path until we add a
# proper hf_xet progress hook — this still streams via the standard tqdm
# wrapper that our patch intercepts. Override-able by the user.
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET", "1")

# ── HF network timeouts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Bound HF network ops so a stalled metadata HEAD or a dead download socket
# RAISES (and surfaces as an error) instead of hanging the model-load worker
# forever — the root cause of the "demo voice spins forever, no error" report
# (most often hit on Windows behind a proxy / firewall / antivirus that wedges
# the multi-GB legacy-LFS transfer). HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT is a *per-read*
# timeout: it resets on every received chunk, so a slow-but-progressing
# download is never punished — only a genuinely dead socket trips it. Both are
# user-overridable for unusually slow links. Set before huggingface_hub is
# imported so its constants pick them up.
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_ETAG_TIMEOUT", "15")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT", "30")

# ── OS trust store for TLS (#976) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Users behind a corporate/antivirus proxy that TLS-inspects HTTPS traffic get
# a raw "[SSL: SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE] ssl/tls alert handshake failure"
# on every model install — the TCP connection succeeds (a different failure
# mode from #984's TCP-level blocked-host case), but the proxy re-signs the
# certificate with its own root CA, which the OS trusts (Windows CryptoAPI/
# SChannel) and Python's bundled `certifi` CA list does not. `inject_into_ssl`
# patches `ssl.SSLContext` process-wide to verify against the OS trust store
# instead, which is the actual fix (not just a nicer error message). Must run
# here — at MODULE level, before huggingface_hub/requests/httpx do any network
# I/O — not inside lifespan(), which runs too late. Not platform-gated: it's a
# correctness improvement everywhere. Best-effort: never block startup.
try:
    import truststore

    truststore.inject_into_ssl()
except Exception:
    pass

# Prevent torchaudio from lazy-importing torchcodec (broken on some installs).
# Proper fix = exclude torchcodec in pyproject.toml; this is a belt-and-braces guard.
os.environ.setdefault("TORCHAUDIO_USE_TORCHCODEC", "0")
sys.modules.setdefault("torchcodec", None)

import warnings
import logg
